title: Choose the visual world
question: The familiar end: three grounded 90s directions and the retro standard. Pick one, or re-roll.

options.label: Table-layout homepage, 1998
options.lineage: Late-90s designed homepages built in FrontPage and Dreamweaver: a centred table, a banner row, a coloured navigation column
options.thesis: The site as a carefully built 1998 homepage: a centred table with a banner row, a navy navigation column and a white reading cell, all in the 216 web-safe colours.
materials: Verdana and Georgia core web fonts
options.viewport: Steel-blue page; a centred table: banner row with the name in embossed type, a navy column holding About, Blog, RSS and the article's contents, and a white cell with the title, meta row and Georgia text.
options.risk: The most generic 90s look: without exact craft it reads as any 1998 small-business site.

options.label: Nerd news portal, 1998
options.lineage: Late-90s engineer news portals (the Slashdot and Freshmeat era): story blocks under coloured title bars, boxed side columns
options.thesis: Every article opens as a story block under a red title bar, flanked by boxed side columns for topics and contents.
options.viewport: Red nav strip and masthead; left column boxes for topics and years; centre: the article as a story block under its title bar; right column box with the table of contents and progress.
options.risk: Busy by nature: three columns of boxes crowd the reading column unless the boxes stay in the margins.

options.label: Generated reference docs, 1998
options.lineage: Late-90s generated documentation (the javadoc era): frames, cell navigation bars, periwinkle summary tables
options.thesis: The site as generated reference documentation: a cell navigation bar, periwinkle header rows opening each section, and a frame listing every article.
options.viewport: A navigation bar of cells with the current one reversed navy; a left frame listing articles by year; the article under a periwinkle title row, its contents as a summary table.
options.risk: Reads as API documentation and Java-flavoured; a post can feel like a class page.

canonCard.label: The familiar retro standard
canonCard.lineage: Measured against 98.css-styled personal sites, Neocities homepages and windows93.net
canonCard.thesis: What retro sites usually ship: every page is a Windows 98-style window on a teal desktop.
canonCard.viewport: Teal desktop with a maximised window: title bar, menu row, the article in a white sunken pane, a blocky progress bar in the status bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from those sites by design; the window chrome costs width on phones and dresses reading up as an operating system.
